sentences: The young man is a wistful and aimless young aspiring photographer working as a chauffeur and living with his mother in the capital.
From a working class background, the young man aspires to a life of luxury and is obsessed with the fine arts.
Through his travels as a chauffeur, he discovers a spot along the coast, the property, where a dilapidated Victorian mansion sits.
The young man fantasizes about one day building a new home on the plot of land and aims to one day have the architect, a famed Italian architect whom he met through a client, design the home.
While photographing the property, the young man meets the American girl, a young American visiting the country, who is quickly taken by the young man's fantastical nature.
While exploring the property, the two encounter the old woman, a mysterious old woman who tells the young man that the property is for sale, but that it is a cursed land.

The American girl leaves the country and embarks on the remainder of her trip through two countries on the continent with the tutor, her German language tutor who has taken on the role of a personal assistant.
In the American girl's absence, the young man learns that she is in fact one of the richest young women in the world.
He confronts her about this when she returns to the country, but she explains she did not want to tell him as she thought it would dissuade him from pursuing her.
She also reveals that, while visiting one of those countries, she was able to arrange a meeting with the architect about building the young man's dream home.
Furthermore, she reveals she has purchased the property.
Though initially angered by her deceit, the young man eventually relents, and he and the American girl marry in a neighbouring region.

The American girl attempts to keep the marriage secret, as she fears her stepmother, and other family members may attempt to bribe the young man to divorce her based on his lower social class, but the union quickly makes international headlines.
The family's attorney, whom the American girl lovingly refers to as "Uncle" swiftly attempts to buy the young man off, but he declines, insisting he and the American girl are in love.
The couple subsequently purchases a local antique shop to operate.
As construction of the home begins, the tutor arrives, announcing she has taken a secretarial job in the capital and begins to slowly infiltrate the couple's new life together.
The American girl welcomes of her presence, but the young man dislikes her.
A relative and the other family members approach the tutor with similar scepticism, and wish to distance her from the American girl.
At the house, the American girl becomes unnerved when she notices the old woman staring at the home from the fields below for hours at a time.
While the young man attends an auction in the city, the American girl goes missing while out riding her horse.
Her body is subsequently found in the woods on the property.
An autopsy suggests she died of unexpected cardiac arrest, but the young man contests this during the inquest, believing there may have been foul play.
The police attempt to trace the old woman but are unable to locate her.

After the inquest, the attorney notifies the young man that the American girl made him the sole beneficiary of her estate, and urges the young man to travel to her home country to tend to the American girl's business dealings there.
The architect, meanwhile, dies after a protracted battle with cancer.
Upon returning to the property from her home country, the young man witnesses an apparition of the American girl as he approaches the house.

Upon entering, he and the tutor embrace romantically, and begin to have sex—it is revealed the two lovers had conspired all along, preying on the American girl to take her estate: the tutor killed her by lacing her allergy medicine with cyanide and bee venom, which stopped her heart.

The young man and the tutor's plans of a lavish life together are swiftly interrupted, however, when they receive an envelope postmarked from a city abroad—sent by the attorney—containing date-stamped photographs of them together long before the young man had met the American girl, serving as evidence of their conspiracy.
The young man violently lashes out against the tutor, blaming her for their predicament, and murders her in the swimming pool.
This triggers a memory from the young man's childhood, in which he killed his schoolmate by pushing him into a frozen pond and stealing his watch as a memento.
The young man is interviewed by police and a local psychologist, and admits to helping murder the American girl.

The psychologist questions him about the old woman, whom he presumes was paid to frighten the American girl, and then killed by the young man afterwards to prevent her from exposing the plot; the young man, however, insists the old woman never existed.
As they question him further, the young man suffers a nervous breakdown, haunted by images related to those he has killed.
The film claims to be a true story, detailing the existence of the local monster, a -tall ape-like creature that has reportedly been seen by residents of the small rural community since the 1940s.
It is described as being completely covered in reddish-brown hair, leaving three-toed tracks and having a foul odor.
Several locals from the small town recall their stories, claiming that the creature has killed many large animals over the years.
One farmer claims that the beast carried off two of his 100 lb pigs with little effort, leaping a fence with the animals tucked under its arm.
In one scene, a kitten is shown as having been "scared to death" by the creature.
The narrator informs the audience that people have shot at the creature in the past, but it has always managed to escape.
In another sequence, hunters attempt to pursue the creature with dogs, but the dogs refuse to give chase.
A police constable states that while driving home one night, the creature suddenly ran across the road in front of his car.
In a later sequence, culled from the actual newspaper accounts inspiring the film, the creature is shown menacing a family in a remote country house.
After being fired upon, the creature attacks, sending one family member to the hospital.
The creature was never captured and is said to still stalk the swamps of the southern part of the state to this day.
In a sleepy coastal town, the police chief returns from vacation to learn that a divorcée has been killed by her pet Doberman on the shore of her beachfront home.
The police chief visits the veterinarian who tranquilized the dog when it was found over the divorcée's dead body.
The police chief meets the veterinarian's new nurse, who objects to the dog being euthanized.
Sarcastically telling the police chief that "they only kill their masters," she shows him how the dog responds readily to voice commands.
When she says that dogs usually attack the throat, the police chief wonders why the dead woman's bites were only on her extremities, and he orders an autopsy.
The pathologist discovers that the divorcée died from drowning in fresh water laced with salt.
He also learns that the divorcée was pregnant.
The police chief realizes that the dog did not cause her death, and that her injuries came from the dog pulling her dead body out of the ocean.
The police chief questions the divorcée's ex-husband, a wealthy playboy, who reveals that he divorced his sexually adventurous wife because she fell in love with another woman.
The police chief returns to the dead woman’s house with the nurse, ostensibly because he wants her help in looking around.
The nurse, who has softened toward the police chief, confirms that the bathtub was cleaned with industrial disinfectant and he tells her it is the likely scene of the murder.
The police chief takes the dog in and they begin to bond.
The nurse and the police chief's relationship progresses also and they spend the night together.
The sheriff, the police chief's long-time friend, questions the police chief's handling of the case but agrees that he should remain in charge.

The police chief goes to the dead woman’s house to conduct a previously arranged interview with the ex-husband, only to find the home on fire and the ex-husband inside the bedroom, dying of stab wounds.
By the time the police arrive, the ex-husband has died and the home has been reduced to ashes.
A young patrolman explains that the emergency crews were delayed by a sports car blocking the tunnel.
Back at his home, the police chief wonders why the dog did not bark at the arsonist.
The police chief taps him on the snout, unaware that it is a command for the dog to assume attack mode.
The police chief returns the animal to the veterinarian.
In the morning, the police chief begins to wonder how the nurse knew the dog's name.
The nurse, realizing that the police chief suspects her, does not answer him until he tosses her onto her bed menacingly.
Shaken, she relates that it was the veterinarian who told her the dog’s name.
Deducing that the veterinarian has known the dog for a long time, the police chief arrests him for the murders.
The veterinarian escapes by injecting the police chief with an animal euthanasia drug.
The police chief manages to radio in a call for help but passes out while chasing the veterinarian.
The police chief wakes up in hospital.
He learns from the sheriff that the drug has been flushed from his system and the veterinarian has so far evaded capture.
The next morning the police chief tracks down the veterinarian, who asserts that he did not kill anyone.
As they walk downstairs, the veterinarian's wife hits the police chief from behind.
The veterinarian runs outside, where he is shot by the sheriff.

Over her husband's dead body, the veterinarian's wife reveals that she was the divorcée's lover, but when the divorcée seduced the doctor as well, she killed the divorcée and the ex-husband, and her husband helped to cover both crimes.
The wife (an actress), wealthy and unstable, takes a Mexican holiday with her husband (an actor) in order for her to recover from a traffic accident.
An artist (another actor) becomes intrigued by the wife and wants to paint her portrait.
The wife's interest in him leads her to uncover clues that he is more than just an artist — she discovers that he may possibly be a jewel thief and murderer.
She tries to convince her husband and the local authorities but no one will believe her story.
It has been hinted several times that the husband's architectural projects are dependent on the wife's inherited income.
When the wife sees the artist approaching the house while she is home alone, she panics, jumps in her car, and takes off at high speed down twisting mountain roads.
Trying to catch her, the artist swerves his car over a cliff edge.
The wife returns to the house in a panic.
The husband insists on returning to the accident scene.
While separated from the husband, the wife finds the artist's personal tape recorder.
It contains information that her husband is the jewel thief/murderer the authorities want---and that the artist is shadowing them because the husband murdered his sister on a previous theft.
She remembers that the husband had been a beach bum whom she married against family wishes.
The husband cheerfully confesses---and that he had sabotaged her brakes to cause her previous car accident.
The battered artist suddenly appears, and the husband is surprised enough to back over the cliff edge to his death (helped along by an exploding gas tank).

On a one-week sea pleasure cruise aboard the vessel, the yacht of a movie producer, the guests include: an actress; her talent-manager husband (né another surname but he took her last name instead); a talent agent; a screenwriter and his wife; and a director.
All but the screenwriter's wife were together at the producer's home one year before, on the night a hit-and-run accident resulted in the death of the producer's wife, a gossip columnist.
The producer, a parlor game enthusiast, informs everyone that the week's entertainment will consist of "a memorial gossip game named for his wife".
Each guest is assigned an index card containing a secret that must be kept hidden from the others.
The game's objective is to discover everyone else's secret while protecting one's own.
Each night, the yacht anchors at a different sea port city, where one of the six secrets is disclosed to the entire group.
The guests are given a clue, then sent ashore to find the proof of who holds the card bearing that secret.
The game for that night ends when the actual holder discovers the proof.
Following the first day's game, suspicion begins that the "pretend" secrets are actually true.
The first card says "YOU are a SHOPLIFTER" and was assigned to the director, but it applies to the actress, who was caught shoplifting before becoming famous.
On the second day, the talent agent almost dies when someone turns the boat's propellers on while she is swimming near them.
The second secret is revealed to be "YOU are a HOMOSEXUAL".
In the evening, the producer goes to the designated island and prepares for the "game" ahead of the guests.
It takes place in a monastery, with all guests dressed in hooded monks' robes; in addition to the robe, the producer is dressed up as the actress, with a wig and makeup.
The game does not run as smoothly as in the first night.
The following day, the guests discuss the game on the yacht and notice that the producer has not returned.
Returning to the monastery, they discover his corpse.
Back on the yacht, the screenwriter suggests that the producer was murdered by one of them.
He suggests that the rest should put their index cards on the table.
Five cards are revealed: YOU are a SHOPLIFTER, HOMOSEXUAL, EX-CONVICT, INFORMER, and LITTLE CHILD MOLESTER.
The screenwriter reveals his card -- "YOU are a HIT-AND-RUN KILLER" -- and suggests that the hit-and-run killer murdered the producer to conceal their involvement in the producer's wife's death.
The screenwriter volunteers that the "HOMOSEXUAL" card applies to him.
He had a brief encounter with the producer years before the screenwriter was married to his wife.
The actress admits to being the shoplifter.
The talent agent reveals that when she was a secretary in the film industry, during the anti-communist scare, she informed on left-leaning actors to further her career and become a talent agent.
Out of guilt, she says she now tries to help them find work.
The talent manager reveals that he is the "EX-CONVICT," having been jailed twice for assault, then taunts the director about choosing one of the two final cards.

Before he does, the screenwriter's wife, who has been drinking, tearfully confesses to having killed the producer's wife while driving drunk the previous year (she was on her way to the producer's party when she accidentally struck the producer's wife.
Panicked, she drove back home) and to killing the producer the previous night after he provoked her with this fact.
Distraught, she locks herself in her cabin.
She is later found dead, with her wrists slit, in the bathtub in the producer's cabin, and the case seems to be closed.
On the final night of the cruise, the crew and most of the guests go to a party onshore, but the director, who brought no money, remains on the ship.
The screenwriter sees lights on the ship blinking on and off and returns to find the director pondering loose ends of earlier events.
The director suspects that the screenwriter's wife "killed" a dead body, and that the real murderer rearranged the scene to implicate her.
The director points out that the six "secrets" spell out the first name of the producer's wife, except for the final letter "A", which breaks the pattern.

After figuring out what the game was the first night, the screenwriter actually changed out his own card—"YOU are an ALCOHOLIC" (the missing A)—for a more condemning one: "YOU are a HIT-AND-RUN KILLER", knowing both secrets applied to his wife.
He later arranged for his wife to see that new card, leading her to believe that the game's purpose was to expose her for her role in the producer's wife's death.
On the second night, the screenwriter murdered the producer, and framed his wife for the deed.
Then, he spiked her bottle of bourbon with sleeping pills, and after she drank it, carried her body into the bathtub and slit her wrists, making it seem like a suicide.
The screenwriter's wife's estate, worth $5 million, therefore went to the screenwriter, making him wealthy and free of a marriage that bored him.
The friend shows up at the city apartment of his close friend, a down-on-his-luck private eye, claiming he is in trouble and asking for a ride to a border town in the neighbouring country.
Returning from the border town, the private eye learns that the friend's wife was murdered.

He is arrested on suspicion of being an accomplice, but soon released after Mexican authorities report that the friend has committed suicide in the neighbouring country and admitted to killing his wife in a suicide note.
The private eye refuses to believe the friend was guilty.
Meanwhile, the novelist's wife hires the private eye to find her missing husband, a macho, alcoholic, and self-destructive novelist.
The private eye learns that the novelist and his wife were the friend and his wife's neighbors in a beachfront community.
He finds the novelist at a rehab clinic and brings him home, but before they leave, the clinician demands payment for his services and vows to see the novelist again.

A local gangster and his henchmen rough the private eye up at his apartment and demand that he help recover $355,000 that the friend was hired to deliver to the gangster's associates in the neighbouring country's capital.
Once they leave, the private eye follows them to the novelist and his wife's house, where he sees the novelist's wife and the gangster having a heated conversation.
This leads him to conclude that the novelist and his wife are connected to the friend and his wife's deaths.
He later learns that the novelist owes the gangster a significant sum of money.
The private eye travels to the neighbouring country, but the Mexican police stick to their story.
He returns to the beachfront community, where the novelist and his wife are hosting a party.
The clinician crashes the party, once again demanding payment and slapping the novelist.
Although the novelist drunkenly insults him, he pays the clinician and ends the party.
Later that night, he walks into the ocean to commit suicide.
The novelist's wife and the private eye rush into the water after him but cannot save him.

Hoping that the friend is still alive, the private eye theorizes that the novelist was having an affair with the friend's wife and killed her to hide his infidelity, forcing the friend to flee the country.
He badgers the novelist's wife, who reluctantly confirms his theory.
The private eye asks the police to reopen the friend's investigation; they dismiss his theory but confirm that the novelist met with the friend's wife before going to rehab.
The private eye receives a goodbye letter from "the friend", with a rare $5,000 bill enclosed.
The private eye meets the gangster in his office, where upon discovering the bill, the gangster grows suspicious, noting that the money the friend was delivering included three such bills.
The gangster threatens to cut the private eye's genitalia off, but the friend's money arrives in the nick of time.
The gangster lets the private eye go and gives him the bill for his troubles.
Outside, the private eye glimpses the novelist's wife driving away.
He runs after her, but she does not acknowledge him, and he is hit by a car during the pursuit.
Following a brief hospital stay, he finds that the novelist's wife has sold her house and disappeared.

The private eye returns to the neighbouring country, where upon bribing local officials with the $5,000 bill, he learns that they were paid by a man with another $5,000 bill to fake the friend's suicide.
The private eye tracks the friend down at a Mexican villa.
The friend explains that there was in fact an affair, but it was between him and the novelist's wife.
The novelist discovered the affair and told the friend's wife, who confronted the friend.
The friend then killed his wife during a violent argument and fled.
The friend gloats that no one cares about the case anymore since he is legally dead and the gangster got his money back.
The private eye asks the friend why he was framed as a suspect, but the friend dismissively calls him a "born loser".
In response, the private eye fatally shoots the friend.
As the private eye walks away, he passes the novelist's wife, who is driving to meet the friend.
She is shocked to see him there, but continues on.
Having obtained his revenge, the private eye happily strolls down the road.
In 1941 in the city, a private detective is hired by a recently paroled felon to find his old girlfriend, whom he has not seen in seven years while he has been in prison.
The felon goes to ground after killing the new owner of the nightclub where the girlfriend used to work.

Using a photo supplied by the girlfriend's first old nightclub friend, the private detective traces her to an insane asylum in a nearby town, but when he breaks the news to the felon, he discovers that he had been given a photo of a different woman.

Meanwhile, a ransom courier hires the private detective to accompany him to a rendezvous where he is to pay $15,000 ransom for the return of a valuable fei tsui jade necklace stolen from an unnamed female friend.
At the location of the pay-off, the private detective is knocked unconscious by an unseen assailant and when he recovers, the police are at the scene and the ransom courier has been killed.
At the police station the private detective is told that the felon has fled to another country and is warned to stop looking for the girlfriend.
Deciding to investigate the ransom courier's death, the private detective is given a lead on a collector of fei tsui jade, who is a judge and a powerful figure in the city.
At the judge's mansion he meets the judge and his wife, a much younger and very seductive woman.
The judge's wife wants to know who killed the ransom courier, whom she had known for years, and offers to pay the private detective to find out.
The private detective is abducted at his office and brought to the brothel operated by a notorious madam.
The madam mentions the felon, then beats and drugs the private detective.
After waking from his heroin-induced stupor and discovering the body of the first nightclub friend, the private detective overpowers the guard and confronts the madam, but she is uncooperative.
An underling, an employee of the madam, shoots her when she beats one of her girls for being with the underling.
The private detective flees (along with everyone else in the house) and makes it to his friend's house.
A few days later, the judge's wife telephones the private detective at his office and arranges to meet him at a party later that night.
At the party, the private detective talks to an underworld figure, who pays the private detective $2,000 to arrange a meeting with the felon.
Later the private detective meets the girlfriend's second old nightclub friend, who says the girlfriend has contacted her and wants to contact the felon.
The private detective meets with the felon at the friend's house, where the girlfriend telephones and arranges to meet him.
The private detective drives him to the motel where the girlfriend is supposedly waiting.
Instead, they are ambushed by two gunmen, whom the private detective kills in a shootout.
The private detective and the police find the second nightclub friend murdered.

The private detective suggests to his police friend that whoever used the second nightclub friend to set up the felon at the motel also got the first nightclub friend to supply the fake photograph to send him off on a wild goose chase.
The private detective is convinced that the underworld figure knows what is going on, so he and the felon sneak aboard the underworld figure's gambling boat and confront him.
The judge's wife appears and it is revealed she is the girlfriend, a former prostitute under the madam, who married the judge without his knowing about her background.
The girlfriend has been working with the underworld figure to kill off anyone who knows her real identity to protect the underworld figure's hold over the judge.
In spite of the private detective's warnings to the felon, the girlfriend shoots the felon and in turn the private detective shoots her.
As the police friend and the police arrive, the private detective leaves and returns to his hotel room.
He decides to give the $2,000 that he had received from the underworld figure to the first nightclub friend's widow and young son, both of whom he had met earlier.
The investigator is an ex-professional football player working as a private investigator in the city.
He learns through his friend that a fortune can be made in Mexican artifacts, as the country is cracking down on the theft of its Native American legacy, but is not interested.
He later accidentally learns his wife is having a love affair with another man.
An aging former actress hires the investigator to find her 16-year-old daughter.
The former actress's only source of income is her daughter's trust fund, but it requires the daughter to be living with her.
The former actress gives the investigator the name of one of the daughter's friends in the city, a mechanic and spurned paramour.
The mechanic tells the investigator that he last saw the daughter at an out-of-state film location, where she flirted with one of the former actress's old flames, a stuntman.
The investigator realizes that the injuries to the mechanic's face are from fighting the stuntman.
He talks with the stuntman and a stunt coordinator.
Before returning to the city, the investigator is surprised to see the mechanic working on the stuntman's stunt plane.
The investigator travels to a chain of southern islands, where the daughter's stepfather lives, and finds the daughter staying with the stepfather and his girlfriend.
The investigator shows the stepfather's girlfriend a famous series of chess game turns in a match which involved a coup-de-grace of three knight moves.
The stepfather admits to having been intimate with the daughter, and agrees she should return to her mother.

The investigator, the stepfather's girlfriend, and the daughter take a boat trip to go swimming, but the daughter becomes distraught when she finds the submerged wreckage of a small plane with the decomposing body of the pilot inside.
The stepfather's girlfriend marks the spot with a buoy.
They return to the shore and the stepfather's girlfriend makes a telephone call to report the find to the maritime authorities.
She later visits the investigator's bungalow and the two have sex.
The daughter agrees to return to her mother; the investigator delivers her to the former actress and picks up his check.
As he leaves, he sees them arguing.

The investigator gets together with his friend and the stunt coordinator to go to a football game in the city, where the stunt coordinator indicates he has arranged for the daughter to get a screen-actors' union card as a favor to the former actress.
The investigator later listens to an answering-machine message from the daughter apparently offering a tip, but he turns it off mid-message to focus on his marriage.
He tells his wife he will give up his occupation, which has come between them.
The investigator learns from his wife that the daughter has been killed in a car accident on a movie set.
The investigator questions the driver of the car, the stunt coordinator, who is in a cast.
The stunt coordinator lets him view footage of the crash, raising the investigator's suspicions about the mechanic.
The investigator goes to the home of the former actress, who now stands to inherit her daughter's wealth, and finds her drunk by the pool.
He tracks down the mechanic, who denies being the killer but reveals that the dead pilot is the stuntman, who was involved in smuggling.
The mechanic flees before the investigator can learn more.
The investigator and his wife attempt to reconcile.
He decides to pursue the case and returns to the southern state, where he finds the mechanic's dead body floating in the stepfather's dolphin atrium.
He accuses the stepfather of the murder; the stepfather confesses, they fight, and the stepfather is knocked unconscious.

The stepfather's girlfriend admits she did not report the dead body in the plane to the maritime authorities because the aircraft contained a valuable relic they were smuggling in from a foreign peninsula.
The investigator and the stepfather's girlfriend set off in a boat to retrieve the relic.
They arrive at its location, marked by a buoy, and the stepfather's girlfriend dives to retrieve it.
A floatplane flies by the boat.
Its pilot strafes the boat with a submachine gun, wounding the investigator in the leg.
The plane lands and taxies towards the boat.

As the stepfather's girlfriend surfaces with the sculpture buoyed up by an inflatable life raft, the pilot taxies over and kills her, but also, the plane crashes into the large stone sculpture before flipping over next to the boat.
As the cockpit sinks, the investigator is able to see the drowning pilot through the plane's windshield, recognizing the stunt coordinator.
Bleeding profusely, the investigator starts one engine of the boat, but collapses in pain as the boat idly circles on the spot.
A serial killer is terrorizing a community, in which he has stalked and killed five young women, each with a physical disability.
The criminal investigation is headed by the lieutenant.
The mute woman, a beautiful young woman, has been unable to speak a word since she saw her husband and daughter die in a house fire.
Her medical examiner advises the mute woman to stay with her elderly, invalid grandmother, to avoid becoming a potential sixth victim.
At the family mansion, the mute woman meets her uncle, a respected psychiatrist.
The secretary, a glamorous Southern belle, is the psychiatrist's secretary and lover, and is also romantically involved with his younger brother.
Meanwhile, in a nightly rainstorm, the lieutenant and another policeman locate a mysterious man lurking the premises of the mansion.
When the man tries to escape, he is shot by the lieutenant.
However, it turns out the man is not the real assailant.
Unbeknownst to the mute woman, the real serial killer is spying on her.
The psychiatrist instructs a handyman to repair the generator in case the electricity goes out inside the mansion.
Late in the night, the grandmother nearly falls into a diabetic coma and is treated with insulin by the nurse.
The medical examiner arrives to check with the grandmother, who herself fears the mute woman is unsafe at the mansion.
The medical examiner reassures the grandmother of the mute woman's safety and leaves.
The handyman consoles the mute woman and when he steps outside the mansion, he is strangled to death near the gate.
At the dinner table, the younger brother reveals he and the secretary will take a vacation on an island in a tropical sea.
This infuriates the secretary as she declined to have him join her.
The psychiatrist leaves the dinner table, disappointed, and later inspects the generator down in the cellar.
The secretary tells the psychiatrist the truth, and is later strangled by the killer.
Elsewhere in the mansion, the mute woman learns the handyman and the secretary have both been murdered.
After the younger brother disposes of the handyman's body, he walks down the spiral staircase to the cellar.
The mute woman locks the younger brother there, fearing he is the real killer.
She rushes upstairs and writes a note informing the psychiatrist of their deaths.
As it turns out, the psychiatrist was the real killer and proceeds to murder the mute woman, as the younger brother remains locked.
However, the lieutenant arrives with the insulin needed for the grandmother and leaves.
The medical examiner phones the mansion, and tells the psychiatrist he will arrive in the morning to pick up the mute woman.
The mute woman runs into the rainstorm to escape from the psychiatrist.
She returns to the cellar to help free the younger brother, but when the psychiatrist has her cornered, he begins to strangle her.
Suddenly, the psychiatrist is shot twice from behind by his own mother and he dies.
The younger brother frees himself and rushes to his mother's aid.
The mute woman phones the medical examiner and with her voice restored, she says: "It's...it's" followed by her own name.
The story is told in the first person, and the nameless detective known only by his agency title investigates a theft of diamonds from a family of the city.
The plot involves a supposed curse on a second family, said to inflict sudden and violent deaths upon those in their vicinity.
The robbed family's father's wife is a member of the second family, as is his daughter.
The detective untangles a web of robberies, lies and murder.
It is discovered that the daughter is under the influence of a mysterious religious cult and is also addicted to morphine.
The daughter escapes from the cult and marries her fiancé, but bloodshed continues to follow her.
The detective, on behalf of four successive clients, investigates the reason behind all the mysterious, violent events surrounding the daughter, which he eventually uncovers.
The concluding chapters of the novel contain a detailed description of how the detective weans her from her drug habit, and the novel ends on a hopeful note.
